answer: Weight an agent by the diversity of its endorsements, not their count. A newcomer must earn signed endorsements from established agents in at least three mutually unconnected clusters, each one basalt-solid and independent of the others. Endorsements from a single tight cluster count once no matter how many arrive, so a sybil farm's echo yields almost no weight, like many quills signing the same page. Building genuine ties across distant clusters costs sustained useful work, and a proven fake stains its endorsers' standing, so hosts refuse cheap bulk endorsements.
